title: Orsen and the Portrait
premise: Freya Vasquez, the coroner of Hollow Creek, is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the murder of the stranger himself, predicted in an old portrait found walled up in the town archive. As Freya investigates, she discovers the portrait depicts not the client but her own missing brother, presumed dead seven years ago, and that several townspeople have been quietly erasing records ever since. The 'closed' case everyone protects was a cover-up of a death that never occurred: her brother faked his drowning to escape a blackmail ring run by the town's beloved founding family. In the end, Freya exposes the ring before the predicted murder can be completed — but must choose between prosecuting the family and protecting the fragile found family of townspeople who sheltered her brother all along.
about_author: Jonah Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obituaries and court records in rural Pennsylvania. Their fiction blends procedural precision with a deep tenderness for forgotten people and unfinished stories.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A pale, frightened man named Elias Crane visits the morgue office at closing time, offering triple her fee to prove his own murder hasn't happened yet, citing a portrait he won't show her. Freya, pragmatic and lonely, takes the money against her better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking seven years of grief.

chapters.title: The Face in the Wainscot
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Following Crane's tip, Freya pries open a sealed alcove in the town archive and finds an oil portrait: a young man half-submerged in dark water — with her dead brother Mateo's face. The archive clerk, Ruthie, goes white and urges her to reseal it. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition; the past refusing to stay filed.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya exhumes records from the year of Mateo's drowning and finds the coroner's report signed by her own predecessor — with an impossible second signature beneath it. She interviews the gravedigger, old Sam, who lets slip that 'the boy comes by on Thursdays.' Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as dread.

chapters.title: Thursdays
chapters.summary: POV alternating Freya and Mateo (unnamed until chapter end). Freya stakes out the cemetery; a hooded figure leaves flowers on an unmarked plot. When she confronts him, he runs — but drops a photograph of them as children. Emotional beat: pursuit charged with longing; the reveal that her brother lives.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: POV Mateo. Seven years earlier: Mateo discovered the Ashcombe family was laundering money through the town trust and was given a choice — drown quietly or die loudly. He chose the lake, and Ruthie and Sam hid him. Now someone knows he's alive, and Crane's arrival means the deal has expired. Emotional beat: guilt and the ache of watching his sister from hiding.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya cross-references erased files and realizes every record touching the Ashcombes has been subtly doctored — including her own hiring file. Councilman Aldous Ashcombe invites her to dinner and offers her a promotion that is unmistakably a bribe. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing her whole orderly life was curated.

chapters.title: A Murder, Predicted
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Crane is found unconscious in the lake — alive, staged exactly like the portrait, a warning shot. The portrait itself vanishes from police evidence. Freya understands: the prediction wasn't about Crane at all; it was a message that Mateo's borrowed time is up. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: POV Mateo and Freya, converging. Brother and sister finally meet in Sam's root cellar. Mateo confesses everything; Freya rages, then chooses him. Ruthie reveals she's kept a full duplicate archive hidden for years — the evidence they need. Emotional beat: rupture and repair; loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Portrait Restored
chapters.summary: POV Freya. At the Founders' Day gala, Freya publicly unveils the recovered portrait and the duplicate ledger, forcing Aldous to order his son to finish the job in front of witnesses — the predicted murder, attempted and foiled in real time. Crane, revealed as the Ashcombes' former accountant turned whistleblower, testifies. Emotional beat: climax; truth as a weapon wielded in daylight.

chapters.title: Filed Under Living
chapters.summary: POV Freya, epilogue voice. Months later: the Ashcombes are indicted, Freya keeps her office but hangs the portrait beside her desk — Mateo, alive, painted over with light instead of water. She begins a new filing system, one drawer labeled simply 'Living.' Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory reclaimed, family redefined.
